summary: Sprint 17A retest after fixes. Both previously failing bugs are now RESOLVED. (1) Memory bias bumped 35→60 in creative_director.py — burger_neon_diner is now Best Match (rank=Best Match, stars=5, reason='Matches your saved style.') for the cross-category sports item appetizers::chicken-wings-12, verified via curl AND the frontend Review step (FIRST card in cd-recs-grid = cd-rec-burger_neon_diner). (2) Download button converted to <button> + triggerDownload() synthetic <a> + setTimeout(0) — the save-style-modal now PAINTS in ~40ms on first click (well under the 500ms target), confirm fires PUT /api/design-memory/{item_key} returning 200, modal closes, askedToSave guard prevents re-open on subsequent download clicks in the same session. Backend pytest 15/15 PASS (test_design_memory.py including the new test_recommend_memory_wins_across_categories). All 11 prior regression flows (menu picker, banner, recs, all-themes toggle, full generate flow) still pass.
critical_code_review_comments: Note (not a blocker): promptSavePreferredStyle at PhotoToFlyer.jsx:974 still early-returns when themeUsed === savedMemory.theme. This is correct behavior (skip prompt if nothing changed), but it means the modal is intentionally NOT shown after 'Use Saved Style' flow. To test Fix #2 end-to-end the prior memory must be absent OR a different theme must be picked manually. The Fix #2 spec is satisfied as written.

Minor: when Use-Saved-Style is active and recs are fetched, the saved theme is also rendered in cd-recs-all-themes — minor visual duplication (saved card appears both at position 0 AND in the expanded all-themes list). Cosmetic only.

rca_of_the_issue: Both bugs fixed cleanly. Fix #1 RCA: memory bias was +35 but category match was +50, so saved theme could not win cross-category. Fix raised bias to +60 — now strictly outranks category. Verified by 2 backend tests + frontend UI. Fix #2 RCA: a real <a href=url download> click handed control to the browser's file-save handler before React could paint the modal. Fix converts to <button>, programmatically synthesizes an <a> click for the download, and defers setSaveModal via setTimeout(0) — modal now paints in 40ms with no race condition. Verified end-to-end (PUT 200, modal closes, no re-open).
